title: Garden Salad with Chicken or Turkey, Bacon and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Garden Salad combines fresh greens (lettuce, spinach, arugula), vegetables (tomato, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper) and protein-rich ingredients: chicken or turkey breast, crisp bacon and grated cheese. The dish is served without dressing, letting the natural flavors shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are lean sources of complete protein, containing all essential amino acids.
Bacon adds a smoky aroma and a modest amount of saturated fat that enhances the salad’s flavor profile.
Hard cheese (e.g., cheddar or parmesan) enriches the dish with calcium and B‑vitamins.
Leafy greens are packed with phytochemicals that provide antioxidant protection.
Skipping dressing keeps the salad low‑calorie and allows precise control of salt and fat intake.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken or turkey supplies essential protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Greens and tomatoes provide vitamin C, vitamin K, folate and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, essential for strong bones.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Carotenoids from carrots and lycopene from tomatoes help combat free radicals.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: Bacon contains monounsaturated fats that, in moderation, can aid cholesterol balance.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium content
items.content: Bacon and cheese can increase intake of saturated fats and salt; people with hypertension should limit them.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Chicken and turkey must be fully cooked to avoid salmonella.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Bacon and cheese are calorie‑dense; over‑consumption may lead to excess energy intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled. Toss the greens with chopped vegetables, add sliced cooked chicken or turkey, crumble crisp bacon and sprinkle grated cheese on top. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice or a light drizzle of olive oil can be added if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Store bacon and cheese separately to prevent the greens from becoming soggy.
